Wallet analysis: model results

These are the saved outputs of the completed full-data run, with the updated logistic coefficient and random forest Gini importance comparison. The plots below compare logistic regression and random forest, each with baseline predictors alone or with five prior-24-hour history features. The original test period has already been inspected, so comparisons remain exploratory.

Reading saved real-data results. No models are fitted or evaluated in this notebook.

Random forest tuning parameters

For each feature set, we randomly sampled 8 parameter combinations from the 27 possible combinations below. Every candidate used the same two chronological, event-purged forward cross-validation folds. Selection minimized row-weighted cross-validation log loss; test outcomes were not used to select settings.

ParameterValues consideredSelected value
max_depth6, 12, or NoneNone — no explicit depth limit
min_samples_leaf10, 25, or 5050 observations per leaf
max_features"sqrt", 0.7, or 1.0"sqrt" — consider a random subset of predictors at each split

max_features=0.7 considers approximately 70% of predictors at a split; 1.0 considers all predictors. All five feature sets selected the same parameter combination. The 200 trees were fixed, not tuned.

Final forest configuration

RandomForestClassifier(
    n_estimators=200,
    max_depth=None,
    min_samples_leaf=50,
    max_features="sqrt",
    criterion="gini",
    bootstrap=True,
    class_weight=None,
    random_state=20261019
)

Gini impurity was used for splits; bootstrap sampling was enabled and no class weighting was applied. The classification threshold stayed fixed at 0.5. The same eight candidates and fold definitions were used across all five feature variants.

Notebook 03: held-forward test outputs

All rows below use the same 26,507 wallet-market observations from October 4–5. The positive-label rate is 59.11%. Accuracy uses threshold 0.5. Higher ROC-AUC and average precision are better; lower log loss and Brier score are better.

History improves the tested forests relative to RF baseline. The +5 prior-24h forest has the highest observed accuracy, while logistic regression has better ROC-AUC and probability-loss metrics. These results do not establish an overall random forest improvement.

Notebooks 02–04: updated individual variable importance

Logistic: absolute standardized coefficients for continuous predictors. RF: Gini mean decrease in impurity. These are rankings within each model; the numerical scales are different. All three price terms appear separately and share highly correlated information.

This comparison uses the saved final models fitted on 52,888 rows. Missing indicators remain unscaled in logistic and are excluded from its continuous-feature ranking; they remain in the fitted models.

Supporting check: grouped validation permutation importance

This earlier plot uses development models fitted on 39,659 rows and outer-validation data. A larger positive score means a greater increase in validation log loss after shuffling the feature group. Price, price², price³ and the price-missing flag move together. Error bars are shuffle standard deviations, not p-values or confidence intervals.

All numeric outputs, including paired descriptive comparisons, are included under results_data/.

Interpretation limits

The target is reconstructed conditional gross profitability, not verified net profit or trading skill. High entry price can help predict frequent small positive outcomes without implying high expected returns. Observed market age is time since the first observed trade, and elapsed study days is not weekday. Model importance is not statistical significance or causality. The test period has been reused and these comparisons remain exploratory.
